title: Derivative along a Gaussian rotation curve
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fréchet derivative $L$ at $x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $\theta\mapsto f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)$ has derivative $L(y)$ at $\theta=0$.
replaced: Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $L$ at $x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $\theta\mapsto f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)$ has derivative $L(y)$ at zero.
